what: the round that merged the four ports and the sentence fixes, made the shared decisions once, closed the guard and tools holes, and froze version 3.3 at thirteen languages

digest.part: Brief 7 round (stage s3c): merge of the four wave-1 ports (perl, swift, ocaml, lua) with the sentence-round fixes, the fourteen shared decisions made once, the guard (G1-G8) and tools (T1-T6) holes closed, a parallel tools round (t7) on the sentence check's identity holes, and the freeze of version 3.3 at thirteen languages (tag v33-frozen = 0065f1e2, tools v33-frozen-tools = d3b258d). Records read in full: brief.md, brief7.md, s3c-merge1.txt, s3c-n-guard.txt, s3c-n-tools.txt, s3c-n-shared.txt, s3c-freeze33a.txt, s3c-t7.txt, s3c-freeze33.txt. Referenced by these records but not given to me: s3c-survey.md (the ten-reader runtime survey), s3c-sfix-shared.txt, s3c-sfix-verify.txt, s3b-wave1-consolidated.md.

rounds.purpose: After four ports (perl, swift, ocaml, lua) were made from the v3.2 guide, reviewed, fixed and verified, merge them, make shared changes once, and close the holes the reviewers found. It sets a rule: what a porter can decide by hand is not a check. A wrong fact, a call the runtime lacks, or a vanished sentence must fail in the guard or tools before any hand record is read.
rounds.who: Plan only. It names the stages: merge, survey (ten readers, two runtimes each), three engineers (guard, tools, shared), freeze, base.
rounds.produced: 14 shared decisions (all additive, optional facts), guard items G1-G8, tools items T1-T6, and a perl lane change.
rounds.changed: It records that no port needed a breaking interface change, but reviewers found pages that were wrong although every check passed, and checks that passed a wrong port. Almost all of those were caught only as open classes in the comparison with the old page, which the porter then decided by hand.

rounds.purpose: Put the four ports and their records on the v3.2 base on one clone, so that thirteen languages stand together. Nothing else was to change.
rounds.who: One merging engineer. Each port's screen was compared byte for byte with its verifier's log, and the swift screen with the in-progress verify log and the fixer's final log.
rounds.produced: Tag v33p = cd8196db, tools 1c97282. 10 source commits were cherry-picked with no conflicts. Trailers were stripped from 2 commits. The six port golden commits were left out and the golden was regenerated once.
rounds.changed: Nothing was decided. perl was left failing on purpose on its 14 defect classes (13 rootquick, 1 reference), which wait for shared changes.

rounds.purpose: Make the guard fail, naming the fact, on every attack the reviewers ran (G1-G8), and add accounts for the new facts.
rounds.who: One guard engineer, from v33p. Their reading of the runtimes was independent of the survey, which they did not read.
rounds.produced: 11 commits touching only the guard test files and forms (26 files, +1051/-100, plus a new calls.ts). They ran 37 attacks and the last freeze's 108 mutations, regenerated the runtime table (1277 lines), and staged ahead citations for facts not yet declared.
rounds.changed: Forms files were forced to change: all 13 provider forms gained `calls`, 12 absences now search the whole runtime, and 5 forms pin type words. The engineer found and fixed their own regression, which had briefly hidden ocaml m07.

rounds.purpose: Close T1-T5 in the review tools, and re-key the four ports' records to the sentence round's identity.
rounds.produced: Tools branch ntools, HEAD d6eabfc, 9 commits. New pieces: callcheck.js (a printed-call check), enumgen.js (minimal-pair judgement of enumerated facts), name-surgery purity, the absent list for a language alone in its result style, and a fix to handstale. The self-test reached 231 controls.
rounds.changed: T6 was not done: the sentence round's independent check did not exist yet. The new checks opened decisions in ts, go, elixir, rb, perl, swift, ocaml and lua. The engineer listed them and decided none.

rounds.purpose: Bring the four ports onto the sentence round's clone (v33s) and make brief 7's 14 decisions in shared code. Also make the perl lane change and declare the new facts in the providers.
rounds.who: One shared engineer. They ran root quick starts from the repository root, on OLD and on NEW, where toolchains existed.
rounds.produced: Tag v33m = cda43a59 (ports on v33s), final HEAD 76779043. Twelve decisions were made in code. Decision 5 needed no change, and decision 10 had already been settled by the sentence round. The perl example test now runs each block from its page's directory. rb's root import was made place-aware too.
rounds.changed: The record is ok: false. The suite had 15 failures. 14 of them were in runtimefacts, where the guard had no account for the new facts or no citations for them. The shared engineer did not write those accounts, because the files belong to the guard engineer. Three interface changes were marked breaking (decisions 12, 13 and 14).

rounds.purpose: Merge the guard onto v33m, bring the tools together, decide the openings in the thirteen languages, and apply what the sentence round's independent check required of the tools.
rounds.who: One freeze engineer. They re-ran the guard engineer's 37 attacks and 108 mutations as an independent check.
rounds.produced: Tag v33a = 21397ef9: v33m plus the guard's 11 commits, 3 of which conflicted and were settled as unions. Tools freeze33a, HEAD 6e224b8. Results: 11 PASS, with ts and perl failing on purpose. The tools self-test ran 235 controls with 0 failed.
rounds.changed: Openings were decided: 70 classes by the sentence round's written rules, 19 that keep their v33p decision, and 14 by hand. Recorded facts: go named, elixir and rb bare, ocaml keys bare, perl and lua prints fields. ocaml lost 21 stale records and had 15 reworded. Fixes 1 and 2 of the sentence check (identity) and the second half of fix 3 were passed on.

rounds.round: t7 (tools: the matching holes the sentence check found)
rounds.purpose: Close items 1-3 of the sentence round's independent check: same-fact-path masking; numbers and articles; a sentence dropped from every variation or from one.
rounds.who: One tools engineer, working in parallel with the second half of the freeze. They also attacked items 4 and 5, which the first half had done, as an independent check.
rounds.produced: Tools branch t7, HEAD 225a0de, 6 commits on 6e224b8. Item 1 is in ident.js. Item 2 is a new pagecheck.js. Item 3 adds an absent list on slot forms, with a per-variation DROPPED check. The self-test reached 266 controls with 0 failed.
rounds.changed: Sentence identity did not change, so nothing was re-keyed, and the thirteen languages' rows were identical to the baseline. Items 4 and 5 fell to the engineer's own attacks (2 of 3 on item 4, 3 of 3 on item 5), which were reported and not fixed. The record says the branch must still be brought into the frozen tools; within these records it is not part of v33-frozen-tools.

rounds.purpose: Merge the shared engineer's work onto v33a, make the guard meet the new facts, have all thirteen languages pass, re-run every attack, and freeze.
rounds.who: One freeze engineer. They compared three readings of each new fact (provider, guard and survey) against the runtime line, and re-ran every attack on a copy of the clone.
rounds.produced: Tag v33-frozen = 0065f1e2 and tools v33-frozen-tools = d3b258d. All 13 one commands pass with nothing open. 14 new attacks were all caught. Of the 37 earlier attacks, 31 are caught; of the 108 mutations, 97 are caught. The suite ran 2631 tests with 0 failures.
rounds.changed: The engineer fixed the guard (deleted read, arity, plain-accessor record), closed two guard holes found under attack, declared ts's utility getter copy:false and its name as a field, reworded two shared sentences (direct's Returns and the list sentence), and fixed perl's deleted sigil. They report H1 refuted on its breaking-changes criterion, at about 25-27 breaking changes.

findings.finding: Version 3.3 is frozen at thirteen languages (tag v33-frozen = 0065f1e2, tools v33-frozen-tools = d3b258d). All thirteen one commands pass with nothing open, no defect, nothing unattested and every absent sentence explained. The suite ran 2631 tests with 0 failures, and the guard 77/77.

H1 is refuted on its breaking-changes criterion. The freeze counts about 25 to 27 breaking interface changes since the first four languages, against a limit of about 10. Three of them came in this round (stream signal, swift's unwrap, utility copy), and 2 or 3 of those were caused by newly ported languages. Providers still read no model: purity is 0 open in all 13.

The four ports needed no breaking change when written. But reviewers found pages that were wrong while every check passed: perl's root quick start could not load its module, perl printed HASH(0x...), and shared sentences were false for lua, php and ocaml. Almost all were caught only as open classes that the porter decided by hand. Brief 7's rule followed: what a porter can decide by hand is not a check.
findings.source: brief7.md 'What the four ports showed', 'The rule this round adds'

findings.finding: The 14 shared decisions were each made once, in shared code, and reached every affected language's page through one change. Examples: the stream-signal sentence changed 94 paragraphs in each of 9 languages, and the match-copy sentence 94 in each of 12. The per-language part was a fact declaration. The freeze reads this as support for H3 in this round.

Example lanes pass wherever a toolchain exists: ts 16/16, go 12/12, py 12/12, c 6/6, rust 6/6, rb 49/49, zig 6/6, and perl 7/7 in three models. perl's example test now runs blocks from the directory each page addresses. It fails with "Can't locate DemoSDK.pm" when the root import is removed, which the old lane could not see. lua, swift, ocaml, elixir and clojure have no compiler here and were checked only by structure and by reading.

Running root quick starts from the repository root found that rb's root block had never loaded, on OLD either, and that go's OLD root block was not a program. Both are fixed at NEW. The c and py root blocks still fail, as on OLD, and are recorded as defects.

The guard now fails, naming the fact, on 31 of 37 recorded attacks, and the freeze caught 14 of 14 new attacks. The 108 mutations of the last freeze come out 97 caught and 5 not caught. Under attack the freeze found two more guard holes and closed them: an 'ahead' citation excused a dropped copy fact, and a missing field flag was never checked.

Several kinds of error are still found only by a reviewer. In this round: perl's deleted read printed without its `$`, a new shared sentence that overstated what `list(nil, nil)` does, a citation whose quoted line holds the token but means something else, and prose false under some feature option. Argument order cannot be checked in languages with no compiler here. Every check passed on the first two until the freeze engineer read the pages.

Comparison with the old page cannot judge facts where the old page was itself wrong or used another convention. ocaml keys 'member' and swift entityBy 'Name' agree with OLD (152:0 and 282:0), yet are wrong. They now fail only in the reviewed mode, against a hand decision.

A runtime survey found facts no page stated. The stream reads callopts.signal in 16 of 20 runtimes, although their operations cannot be cancelled. lua and php keep the accessor's instance. ts and js return the live utility object because struct.clone keeps class instances by reference, which was run in node. A quoted clone call is therefore not proof of a copy.
findings.source: s3c-n-guard.txt stream_signal; s3c-freeze33.txt disagreements[1]; brief7.md decision 13

findings.finding: The method has a cost in hand decisions and brittle controls. Merging the sentence fixes into the four ports opened classes, which were decided as 70 by written rules, 19 by carry-over and 14 by hand. ocaml's 38 stale records needed rewording or removal. 16 self-test controls broke only because two paragraphs were re-wrapped.

Holes remain in the review tools. At the freeze, the sentence-identity holes were still accepted (zig .ok/.err swapped, py list(), rb Hash, a wrong step number or article). A parallel round (t7) closed them on its own branch: 266 controls, 0 failed, no change to the thirteen tables. Its own attacks still beat it in 3 named ways, and beat items 4 and 5 in 5 of 6 attacks. Within these records, t7 is not yet merged into the frozen tools.
